themes.name: Release reliability and incident response
themes.summary: The team reported dependable production releases with no rollbacks and coordinated quickly when a customer escalation arrived.

themes.name: Code review turnaround
themes.summary: Review turnaround remains a bottleneck for urgent fixes; the team wants consistent two-reviewer practice from earlier retros.

themes.name: Sprint planning efficiency
themes.summary: Planning sessions exceed ninety minutes; the team proposed time-boxing and async status notes.

strengths.summary: Production releases stayed reliable with no rollback during the sprint.
The team rallied quickly when a customer escalation landed.

concerns.summary: Review turnaround is still too slow for urgent fixes.
Sprint planning sessions routinely exceed ninety minutes.

opportunities.summary: Enforce the two-reviewer policy discussed in earlier retrospectives.
Time-box planning and replace status updates with async notes.

suggestedActions.title: Define a release readiness checklist with automated pre-deploy gates
suggestedActions.reason: The team raised release reliability themes (FB-0001, FB-0002). A shared go/no-go checklist and automated pipeline gates should catch blockers before promote.

suggestedActions.title: Agree an urgent PR first-response SLA and escalation path
suggestedActions.reason: Slow turnaround on urgent reviews was raised (FB-0003, FB-0005). Set a measurable first-response target and escalation when reviewers are unavailable.

suggestedActions.title: Pilot two-reviewer policy exceptions for labeled hotfix PRs
suggestedActions.reason: Urgent review delays and two-reviewer policy appeared together (FB-0003, FB-0005). Pilot hotfix-labeled exceptions with mandatory post-merge review.

suggestedActions.title: Timebox planning sessions and require async pre-reads plus decision logs
suggestedActions.reason: Long planning and async status ideas (FB-0004, FB-0006). Cap live planning and distribute pre-reads before the session.

limitations: Suggested actions require human review before approval.
Analysis identifies process patterns, not individuals.
Observations are not proof of causality.
Anonymous submissions are not attributed to individuals.
